title.narrative: Provision of Life-Saving Integrated Nutrition Interventions to Reduce Malnutrition Among Vulnerable Women and Children in High-Risk LGAs of the Borno and Yobe states

description.narrative: The CERF allocation will enable UNICEF to rapidly respond to the surge in severe acute malnutrition (SAM) among children in the 14 high-risk Local Government Areas (LGAs) with IPC AMN Phases 3 (serious) and 4 (crisis). Since January 2024 there has been substantial evidence of deprivation established by the eight-year high child admissions at outpatient therapeutic programmes (OTP) and Stabilization Centers (SCs). A nutrition situation analysis conducted by the UNICEF MFO Nutrition Section indicated a 48 per cent increase in total SAM admissions to OTPs and SCs across Borno, Adamawa and Yobe (the ‘BAY’ States) in the first quarter of 2024 compared to the same period in 2023. The observed pattern is expected to continue and worsen during the lean season in 2024 since the aggravating factors are not predicted to improve. UNICEF and the nutrition sector in the BAY states estimated over 1.5 million children with wasting and 511,807 suffering from severe wasting in 2024. Hence, this support will focus the resources on extremely hard-to-reach areas with severe needs, addressing food and nutrition security challenges to improve nutrition outcomes in the targeted LGAs. UNICEF’s nutrition response will emphasize life-saving nutrition interventions while strengthening preventive activities in the 14 high-risk LGAs. The project will target 500,000 beneficiaries for active case finding to enable timely identification and referral of children under 5 years old with SAM to outpatient therapeutic feeding programs (OTPs) for appropriate nutritional care. Specifically, 50,199 children (23,099 boys and 27,100 girls) with SAM without medical complications will be admitted to OTPs. Additionally, 117,000 women and 13,000 men will receive preventive nutrition services, such as counseling on optimal infant and young child feeding practices, in collaboration with local NGOs capable of accessing hard-to-reach areas with IPC levels 3 and 4.
